text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- "Support for Macedonia will not fail at the Donors Conference in Brussels in late February," Macedonian deputy prime minister Jane Miljovski told parliament foreign policy commission, but refrains from forecasting the amount of funds Macedonia can expect. Miljovski said he hoped the donation would be higher this time than in the previous two cases.

- Verification of certificates for imports of food and alcoholic drinks to be stepped up. Imported fake brands of alcoholic drinks found to contain tea, chemicals and petroleum, state inspection service says.

- Macedonian foreign minister Ljubomir Frckoski at meeting with U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said: "The situation in the region is aggravated by the reduction of the number of peacekeepers in Macedonia".

- The ethnic Albanian Party for Democratic Prosperity, dissatisfied with treatment of its ministers in the government coalition, to take final decision on leaving the government by the end of the week, Dnevnik learns from senior party sources.
- Two senior members of the Democratic Party executive board Denko Skalovski and Dragan Gorencev resign over party leader Petar Gosev's decision to integrate the Democratic and Liberal parties.
